structured_output.what_is_happening: This is a fresh pump.fun token called "Eliza" ($ELIZA). It launched about 10:10 UTC, left the bonding curve about 8 minutes later, and is now around $105k market cap on PumpSwap with $28k liquidity. In roughly 11 minutes it drew 1,061 unique buyers against 681 sellers and gained about 113%. The description says creator fees go to Shaw (@shawmakesmagic, the elizaOS founder) through UsePaid, so it is a fee-redirect or tribute token. Its only linked social is a post from @cybermyrix, an X account previously named real_yazar. About 8 other ELIZA/ELIZAOS tokens launched between about 06:20 and 10:10 UTC today and are all dead at about $3k. That cluster hints at some trigger this morning, but I could not identify it. Background: Shaw has publicly stepped away from tokens. He called the ELIZAOS token dead after a lawsuit, Eliza Labs is winding down, and he said he will "never let a token come close to Eliza again".

narrative.description: This is a tribute/fee-redirect meme around Eliza, the elizaOS AI agent brand, with creator fees pledged to founder Shaw. It trades on nostalgia for AI-agent meta and on the chance that Shaw notices or accepts the fees.
narrative.why_spreading: Eliza is a well-known name from the 2024 AI-agent era, and 'fees to the famous dev' tokens can pull in a crowd quickly. Several ELIZA copies launched this morning, which suggests a possible trigger (a Shaw post?) that I could not verify. The main risk is that Shaw has publicly rejected tokens, so he may disavow this one instead of endorsing it.

token_connection.why_this_token: Of today's wave of ELIZA launches, this is the only one that left the bonding curve and has real volume. The others are dead at about $3k market cap. It is the only one pledging fees to Shaw through UsePaid.
token_connection.competing_tokens: There are the old 2024 ELIZA (5voS9...) and lowercase eliza (wUtwj...) tokens at about $130-155k market cap with no volume, plus about 8 dead same-day copies.

authenticity.evidence: On the organic side: 1,061 unique buyers, a 1.4:1 buyer-to-seller ratio, a low bot/degen rate (7%), a low fresh-wallet rate (13%), low snipers and a top-10 holder share of 18.6%. On the other side: 79 bundler wallets (although they hold only about 1.9% of the top traders' share), the creator has already sold and closed out (creator_close), a CTO flag is set, and the social account is recycled (renamed from real_yazar, with 8 deleted token posts). I found no paid DexScreener boosts.
authenticity.uncertainty: I had no X data. The linked post could not be fetched (HTTP 402), and I could not verify whether Shaw has acknowledged the token.

structural_risks: The creator has already exited (creator_close), and the linked X account is recycled with deleted token posts
The token already rose about 113% in its first minutes, so a retrace is likely
Shaw could publicly disavow it, given his stated anti-token stance
RugCheck reports low liquidity of $866, which looks stale; DexScreener shows $28k and the LP is 100% burned

structured_output.counterargument: This could be a routine 'fees to famous dev' pump-and-fade. Shaw has explicitly said he wants nothing to do with tokens, the deployer has already left, and the account behind it is a recycled shill account. The 38% move in five minutes may just be the migration spike, which usually retraces more than 50% as early buyers take profit. On the other side, if a real Shaw post triggered today's wave, this coin is the clear survivor and could move 5x or more.
unknowns: What set off this morning's wave of ELIZA launches
Whether Shaw has acknowledged or claimed the UsePaid fees
What the @cybermyrix post says and how much engagement it has

source_coverage.notes: A search for the contract address returned nothing relevant. The X post returned HTTP 402. The UsePaid page failed with an SSL error. News searches found background on Shaw's anti-token stance, but nothing current that ties to this launch. The time limit prevented Reddit, Telegram and Discord searches.

structured_output.thesis: This is a recognizable brand that won today's copy race, with broad early buying and a clean distribution. It is held back by a creator who has already exited, a recycled promoter account, a figurehead who has publicly rejected tokens, and a large move already made. That makes it above average for this pool, but not by much.
